en.title: oo
en.summary: This is the letter L321 from the vowel-consonant groups.

sections.title: The digraph oo
paragraphs: The letters oo make several different sounds. The main sound is heard in the word (moon) /muːn/, which is the bright object in the night sky. A digraph is two letters that together write one sound, such as sh. This letter group makes four different sounds in English words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, pull your tongue back and make your lips into a small, tight circle. For the second sound, relax your lips and tongue a little. For the third sound, drop your jaw slightly and keep your tongue low and flat. For the fourth sound, drop your jaw more and round your lips loosely. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake on all four sounds.

sections.title: When to use each
paragraphs: The letters oo usually make the long sound before n, l, or m, as in (cool) /kuːl/. They usually make a short sound before k or d, as in (book) /bʊk/. In a few special words like (blood) /blʌd/, they sound like a short open vowel. In words like (door) /dɔː/, they sound like a long open vowel.

sections.title: Watch out for mistakes
paragraphs: Do not use the long sound of (cool) /kuːl/ for words like (good) /ɡʊd/. The vowel in (good) /ɡʊd/ is shorter and your lips stay more relaxed. Do not confuse (blood) /blʌd/ with the vowel in (moon) /muːn/. Say (blood) /blʌd/ with a relaxed, low tongue, exactly like the vowel in the English word cup.
